description: issue #685 (slice I6): registration is not invocation, and a click is host input — a headless batch `execute()` run has no pointer device, so an `on_click [ ... ]` handler is registered (emitting the `instruction`+`primitive` pair, seq 0-1) but never fires. This mirrors I3's `when "stop"` and I5's `on_key` narrowing: the following `print "mid"` runs (seq 2-3) and that is the whole event stream — `"moved"` is never printed. This slice deliberately does NOT synthesize a synthetic click-injection API to make the handler fire; delivering a click belongs to a later interactive host slice. Locking that narrowing with this fixture makes it falsifiable rather than silently omitted.
